record.title: Scientist World reports a benchmark of AI research agents across 1,000 executable paper environments
record.summary: A 5 November arXiv paper introduces Scientist World, which turns selected empirical papers into executable research environments. The authors report releasing 1,000 environments with reproduced baselines, hidden evaluation slices and separate verifier-agent checks. In their benchmark, agents improved on the reproduced method in 84% of improvement attempts and 74% of attempts that designed a method from scratch. The paper also reports raising Qwen3-8B’s median idea score across ten held-out papers after supervised fine-tuning and offline reinforcement learning; a fixed GPT-5.6 Sol implementer executed all ideas. These are author-reported results from the paper’s selected tasks and setup. They do not establish general autonomous scientific discovery, and were not independently audited or reproduced here. The linked project page shows zero indexed/analyzed/selected/future counters but elsewhere advertises 2,079 verified runs and a 76% result against the paper’s 74%. Public MIT system and CLI repositories are now visible; the linked organization currently lists two public repositories, neither for arXiv:2611.08478 and the trace dataset returned HTTP 401. The paper-specific environment and traces remain inaccessible through the inspected links, and the counter/score discrepancy remains unresolved.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A paper submitted to arXiv on 5 November 2026 describes Scientist World, a system that converts empirical research papers into runnable environments by reproducing a paper method, specifying an improvement task and visible/held-out evaluations, packaging the workspace, and passing it to separate verifier agents.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a first release of 1,000 environments selected from 124,816 indexed papers and say the released environments reproduce source-method results within margin in 99% of cases and pass a separate verifier in all 1,000 cases. These validation figures have not been independently audited here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ benchmark, AI-scientist agents beat the reproduced paper method on held-out evaluation in 84% of improve attempts and 74% of innovate-from-scratch attempts. The paper describes a single controlled trial per paper, model and mode; results are benchmark-specific and not external replications of the underlying research papers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that supervised fine-tuning and offline GRPO on research traces improved the median held-out ideation score of Qwen3-8B from 41.2 to 106.3 across ten papers. A fixed GPT-5.6 Sol implementer carried out all 30 ideas under the same conditions, so the result concerns ideation quality under this setup, not end-to-end autonomous research capability.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that agents make novel, durable scientific discoveries in deployed research programs, that the benchmark represents scientific work beyond the selected empirical papers, or that its reported results independently reproduce.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: At the current inspection, the project site’s progress panel showed zero indexed, analyzed, selected or future environments while a separate block advertised 2,079 verified runs and 76%, versus the paper’s 74%. The linked public system repository is MIT-licensed, but its README says environments are separate GitHub repositories named by arXiv ID and separately licensed. The ScientistWorld organization currently lists two public repositories, neither for arXiv:2611.08478; the linked trace dataset returned HTTP 401. Thus the exact paper-specific environment collection and full trace corpus were not accessible through the inspected links, and the counters and 74%/76% figures remain unreconciled.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper-linked public system repository and CLI repository are visible, and the system repository lists an MIT license and commands for use. Its README distinguishes environment repositories from the system code and says environment licenses follow the underlying papers, code and datasets. The linked ScientistWorld organization currently lists two public repositories, neither matching arXiv:2611.08478. A PyPI package page documents a sciworld command-line distribution, but no environment was installed or executed and this does not establish access to the specific claimed collection.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent audit of the released 1,000 environments, reproduction figures or verifier outcomes was performed.
The reported 84%/74% held-out benchmark rates and ideation-training gain have not been reproduced by an independent team.
Generalization beyond selected empirical papers in four arXiv categories and transfer to real research outcomes are not established.

The system repository and CLI are public and list MIT-licensed system code, but the README says environments are separate per-paper GitHub repositories under their own licenses. At the current check, the linked organization lists two public repositories, neither for arXiv:2611.08478; the trace-dataset link returns HTTP 401. The project page’s zero counters and separate 2,079-run/76% block also remain inconsistent with the paper’s 74%. The exact environment/traces and metric relationship are unresolved.

brief.importance_rationale: If the released environments are valid and the reported effects reproduce, converting empirical research papers into executable tasks and using measured outcomes to train research-ideation models could materially change how AI research capability is evaluated and developed. This score reflects possible consequence, not confidence in the results.
limitations: The main benchmark and training results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced here.
Papers were selected by an automated quality/feasibility process from four arXiv categories; the reported results do not cover all scientific fields or all research tasks.
The 74% result is for innovate-from-scratch attempts in this benchmark. It does not mean that 74% of scientific discoveries or papers are independently improved in real research programs.
The Qwen3-8B training result isolates ideation by having a fixed GPT-5.6 Sol implement all generated ideas; it does not test a small model completing the full research loop.
The paper reports 100% verifier approval, but the verifier is another agent in the same automated pipeline rather than an external independent audit of the released corpus.

At the current inspection the ScientistWorld GitHub organization lists two public repositories, neither for arXiv:2611.08478; the paper-specific environment and trace corpus were not accessible through the inspected links. The public MIT license applies to the system repository, not automatically to separate environments.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 1,000 environments, 99% reproduction within margin and 100% verifier approval; held-out improvement over source method in 84% of improve and 74% of innovate trials; and Qwen3-8B median idea score rising from 41.2 to 106.3 after SFT plus offline GRPO over ten papers.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports 239,506 compute jobs and 2,286 GPU-hours across environment construction; median per paper is 0.4 GPU-hours. Each paper may use up to 70 GPU-hours. These author-reported totals do not include an independently audited full lifecycle cost.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible arXiv paper documents the pipeline, author-reported measurements and evaluation design. The linked public system/CLI repositories and sciworld package page document an available software interface, but the paper-specific environment and trace corpus were not accessible through inspected links. The visible GitHub organization lists two other paper repositories. No code was installed or executed, and no independent benchmark or training replication was performed.
technical.mechanism: A multi-agent pipeline reproduces a source method, defines a paper-grounded task and evaluation, packages a portable workspace, and uses separate verifier agents. Research agents act through visible training slices; a held-out slice is materialized only after the method is frozen. A separate training experiment uses outcomes from research traces to train an ideation model.
technical.regime: Selected empirical papers from cs.CL, cs.CV, cs.AI and cs.LG indexed Jan 2025–Mar 2026. Benchmark attempts use specified frontier/open models and fixed compute limits; the training ablation evaluates ten held-out papers with GPT-5.6 Sol implementing ideas.
technical.reproducibility: The arXiv HTML includes methodological and experimental appendices. The linked system and CLI repositories are public; the system repository lists MIT, while its README says the separate per-paper environments retain their own licenses. The ScientistWorld organization currently lists two public repositories, neither for 2611.08478, and the linked trace dataset returned HTTP 401. A PyPI sciworld CLI page is visible, but package availability does not prove this paper-specific environment is accessible. The project page’s zero progress counters and separate 2,079-run/76% block remain inconsistent with the paper’s 74%. No code was installed or run; no independent audit or replication occurred.
technical.strongest_baseline: Each task compares a proposed method with the corresponding paper method reproduced by the builder pipeline. The paper’s reported percentages measure attempts exceeding that reproduced method on held-out slices, not the proportion of papers whose original scientific conclusions were independently validated.

brief.title: Scientist World reports a benchmark of AI research agents across 1,000 executable paper environments
brief.why_it_matters: Executable environments built from prior research could provide a common way to test whether AI agents improve methods through measured experiments and could supply outcome-linked training data. The paper reports a substantial benchmark and training pipeline, but its results depend on author-selected papers, constructed tasks and a particular model/implementer setup. Independent audits are needed before inferring broad research productivity or autonomous discovery.
